batch_strategy: Failure repair with paired condition and loading response experiments, emphasizing late-tail calibration while retaining low-strength anchors and scaffold diversity.

choices.reason: The model predicts a broad late interval for a heteroatom-rich row at 10/1 DCM and high loading. It extends the underpredicted late regime seen for m107 and m118 in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 2d178efe0181baca2bd5.

This high-width 50/1 DCM row tests whether a carbonyl-rich scaffold enters a late regime at larger sample volume. The m177 loading contrast in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 4862e2fb71344ce16021 shows that apparently similar strong-condition rows can have very different tails.

A high-width 10/1 DCM point for an oxygen-rich ester scaffold probes the onset-to-finish transition between ordinary and extreme carbonyl retention, informed by the measured m107 and m118 failures in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 2d178efe0181baca2bd5.

The model gives a very broad upper-tail prediction for a carbonyl-containing aromatic at 50/1 DCM. This is a useful remote-space label because observed oxygen-rich rows such as c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 3163a9b58f1a52a1992c were substantially later than their predictions.

This 10/1 DCM row combines a broad predicted tail with an unusual loading-solvent volume. It tests whether the tail behavior seen in 8de30a7f5764c20b232e and b514312eda7950cdcf1c transfers to a different oxygenated scaffold and loading context.

The model predicts a late, broad interval at 10/1 PE for an alcohol-containing scaffold. It samples a condition family where strong retention and endpoint-specific errors have been observed, while adding a high-volume loading point for generalization.

This high-width 10/1 DCM aldehyde/ester-like row tests a strong-condition upper tail in a scaffold distinct from the measured m195 and m198 examples. It is useful for distinguishing family-specific high-ratio behavior from a global correction.

An intermediate high-strength point for the nitrobenzaldehyde-like family can connect the measured m198 behavior in cdaf95461fe3b3d80075 to stronger-condition rows. Its predicted width indicates potential endpoint calibration value.

This lower-strength m195 point is paired conceptually with the measured high-ratio overprediction in 7654254c03d9de79740f. It tests whether the model's excessive late prediction persists when strength and loading are changed.

A second m195 condition-response point at 20/1 DCM helps separate a scaffold-specific high-ratio anomaly from a smooth solvent-strength trend. The measured 7654254c03d9de79740f provides the high-ratio comparison.

This low-strength m160 anchor tests whether the aminobenzonitrile late-retention regime has a threshold in solvent strength. The measured 5/1 failure in ad833f34f6b91872362d motivates an explicit low-strength point.

The corresponding low-strength m161 point supplies an isomer-matched control for the m160 experiment. It is valuable because ad833f34f6b91872362d and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f show unexpectedly late behavior for both isomers under stronger conditions.
This m161 1/1 DCM point tests the transition between the low-strength floor and the known late 5/1 regime. It adds a volume contrast to the isomer evidence in a60552f4d1a5ced4641f.

The matched m160 1/1 DCM row complements the m161 point and tests whether positional substitution changes the loading and solvent response. The observed m160 label in ad833f34f6b91872362d is a strong reason to repair this local family.

This m160 5/1 row uses twice the sample volume of the known catastrophic point in ad833f34f6b91872362d. It directly tests whether the late regime is primarily condition-driven or amplified by loading amount.
The same 2/1 m200 condition at a different sample volume is a controlled loading-response experiment. It extends the measured m200 tail behavior and tests whether V2 scales independently of V1.

This high-ratio m208 row samples an upper-tail regime with a large predicted endpoint interval. It extends measured m208 condition-response behavior into a stronger solvent condition and helps calibrate high-strength heteroatom effects.

A high-strength PE experiment on an alcohol-containing nitroaromatic provides a chemically different late-tail probe. It tests whether the strong predicted tail is transferable across loading and solvent systems.

The model predicts a broad late interval for oxygenated m116 at 50/1 DCM. This row probes a methoxy-rich family in which high-ratio response may be nonlinear and helps distinguish V1 from V2 correction needs.

This high-width m115 point provides a strong-condition carbonyl/aryl ether label at larger volume. It complements the broader oxygen-rich failures in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and tests upper-tail transfer across related carbonyl scaffolds.

A donor-free aromatic carbonyl row at 50/1 PE supplies a control for whether strong-condition corrections require heteroatoms or also occur in less polar graphs. It helps discriminate the family-specific behavior seen in 6d5c9e3367e3d9b87fe4 and 3f79435038d038b87d4f.

This high-ratio m26 row targets a carbonyl-rich aromatic with a broad predicted V2 tail. It samples a distinct scaffold while retaining similarity to observed high-ratio carbonyl failures, supporting transferable upper-tail calibration.

The 20/1 DCM m114 point tests whether a late finish develops before the most extreme 50/1 condition. It complements the measured 50/1 m114 behavior in 0cf0d36290765378ae8d and separates condition strength from loading effects.

This 5/1 DCM m37 row probes a moderate-strength nitroaryl carbonyl regime between ordinary and extreme tails. The measured m37 rows in b6f1b33a5491968c645e and 9ae9c8b491a04e429a11 show that this family can be substantially later than predicted.

A low-strength, high-loading m38 anchor tests whether loading alone can produce a broad finish interval. It complements the measured higher-strength m38 tail in d1e922c04dbd0c9f6c06 and calibrates the early-elution floor.

This m173 point combines a large loading-solvent volume with a broad predicted V2 interval. It extends the measured m173 condition-response labels in 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286 and b37608f8c4a8ee4b8696 into a higher-strength, high-loading regime.

The matched lower-strength m173 point creates a meaningful response curve with 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8. It can identify whether the large V2 tail is caused by solvent strength, loading, or their interaction.

This high-loading m99 row tests whether the long finish observed in the measured 10/1 m99 experiment d8f34dc388842e55905b persists when sample volume is increased. It is a direct loading-sensitivity label for a polar ester/alcohol-like graph.

The high-ratio m117 point is a controlled low-volume complement to measured m117 rows a0d6732883ffc7d063fb and d9c8c8af50a10bf07765. It targets the model's uncertainty about whether V2 growth survives reduced loading.

This m193 20/1 DCM point increases sample volume relative to measured m193 rows c28747d70e7b51a1cc95 and a5f9179bfb146ad70953. It tests a loading-dependent tail in a nitroaryl aldehyde family with broad endpoint predictions.

A low-strength m206 anchor is useful because the measured stronger-condition m206 row 614873124b33029a924c was much later than its prediction. This point tests whether the anomaly begins only after increasing eluent strength.

This low-strength m31 anchor complements the measured high-strength m31 behavior in b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11. It tests whether the observed late shift is a solvent-strength response or a scaffold-independent model bias.

hypotheses.content: High-loading, polar or heteroatom-rich graphs form a late-retention regime that the current model often underpredicts, especially for V2; the effect is substantial but scaffold-specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These failures affect both endpoints and occupy broad regions of the Row-distribution, so labels that distinguish ordinary from late retention can improve representation, condition response, and upper-tail calibration.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the late regime recur across unrelated polar scaffolds at matched strength and loading, or is it confined to a few molecular families?

hypotheses.content: V2 tails can change independently of V1, and loading amount or loading-solvent conditions interact with solvent strength to control that tail.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: QGeoGNN needs labels that separate onset calibration from finish calibration; paired loading and condition rows can teach this interaction more efficiently than isolated high-width rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: For a fixed scaffold and mobile-phase strength, does changing loading primarily move V2, V1, or both?

hypotheses.content: High-ratio condition response is scaffold-specific; donor-free, oxygenated, sulfur-containing, and fused graphs do not share one transferable correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A global solvent-strength adjustment would worsen some families while helping others; explicit cross-family labels can encourage the model to learn interaction terms instead.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural features determine whether increasing PE/EA ratio produces early elution, a late tail, or an anomalous floor?

hypotheses.content: Aminobenzonitrile retention is strongly sensitive to substitution environment and condition, so positional isomers should not be pooled through generic polarity descriptors alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This family exposes a representation failure with very large V1 and V2 errors; matched low-strength and intermediate-strength labels can teach substitution-specific condition response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the two aminobenzonitrile isomers share a common retention threshold, or do their late transitions occur at different solvent strengths and loadings?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measured outcomes strengthened the separation between onset and finish learning. The m177 pair b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 4862e2fb71344ce16021 showed that a broad V2 tail can depend strongly on loading even when V1 stays near the early-elution floor. The aminobenzonitrile labels ad833f34f6b91872362d and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f confirmed a severe, isomer-sensitive underprediction regime. At the same time, 7654254c03d9de79740f showed that a fused aldehyde can be overpredicted at high ratio, so predicted width alone cannot justify a global late-retention correction. The batch therefore uses paired response points, family controls, and low-strength anchors alongside broad-width exploration.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs several measured failure regions while preserving coverage across carbonyl-rich, nitro, amino, alcohol, ester, fused, donor-free, and heteroatom-containing graphs. High-width rows target upper-tail calibration where observed labels show large V2 errors. The m160/m161, m195, m173, m99, m117, m193, and m206 selections form local condition or loading-response experiments rather than redundant replicates. Low-strength m31, m38, m160, m161, and m206 anchors test whether late behavior has a threshold and help calibrate early-elution floors. The remaining high-ratio controls test whether corrections depend on scaffold class. Together these labels can improve generalization by teaching QGeoGNN separate V1 and V2 responses, loading interactions, and chemically conditional solvent-strength effects across the Row-distribution.
